scenes.heading: Editing workflow that doesn't burn you out

sents.d: Editing workflow that doesn't burn you out
A repeatable editing system prevents backlog and burnout.
Editing backlog is one of the most common reasons photographers burn out — treating each gallery as a fresh creative project instead of following a repeatable process makes the workload feel endless.

A consistent culling process (rejecting clearly unusable shots first, then selecting favorites, rather than agonizing over every frame individually) speeds up the first and most tedious stage significantly.
Batch-applying a base edit across similar lighting conditions, then only fine-tuning standout images individually, typically cuts total editing time well below editing every image from scratch.

take: Cull quickly and batch edits instead of perfecting every frame.
